name: pdk-gnocchi-online-sack-resize
instr:
# Goal

`gnocchi-change-sack-size` currently refuses to resize Redis incoming sacks with a backlog, and long-running API processes retain the old sack count. Make an 8-to-64 sack resize work while ingestion and metricd keep running. Work in `/app`; keep the existing Gnocchi HTTP and CLI interfaces.

# Requirements

1. A resize invoked with `gnocchi-change-sack-size --sacks-number 64` succeeds within 30 seconds even with pending measures. Every measure accepted by either running API process before, during, or after the resize contributes exactly once to its metric's `sum` and `count` aggregates.
2. API processes started before the resize write to the current layout without restart within 30 seconds of the resize command returning; a process suspended across the resize must do so within 30 seconds of being resumed. Once the resize has returned and metricd is running, old sacks are drained and retired within 60 seconds, not merely scanned indefinitely.
3. Old and new pending measures for one metric are applied without losing earlier points to an archive policy with `back_window: 0`, even when the newer point is more than two blocks later. No concurrent aggregate writers for the same metric across `gnocchi-metricd` and `refresh=true`, including while an S3 write is slow. A running `gnocchi-metricd` aggregates pending measures within 45 seconds, and every API request, including `refresh=true`, returns within 35 seconds.
